reason: The measurement of the quiet marks is right and the load-bearing comparison built on top of it is wrong, and the fix inherits the error. Verified in chromium at 1440 in both grounds: --mark-ctx is #d4d4d8 at :41 and #3f3f46 at :100, .bar at :241 and .dot::before at :357 paint exactly those, the ground under both is var(--paper) = #ffffff / #18181b, eleven of twelve columns carry class "bar" and six of nine dots carry no .old, and the ratios are 1.48:1 and 1.70:1 as claimed. Both gates are blind as claimed: audit.mjs's contrast pass is gated on hasText && visible and never reaches a fill, and interaction-check.mjs has no non-text rule at all (its only contrast assertion is the lead-plate numeral at :1175). So far the seat is correct. WHAT IS WRONG: the finding's scale argument -- "the live indigo column at 6.29:1 light and 5.94:1 dark, so the surface is carrying a fourfold contrast gap" -- measures .bar.live, and .bar.live paints in ZERO states. Driven across all seven (full, partial, quiet, first-run, empty, loading, error) the count of .bar.live is 0 every time, because chart() at :714 reads w.partial ? "bar part" : (live ? "bar live" : "bar") and the twelfth week is partial:true in the fixture for every scope. The mark that actually paints is .bar.part: hatched Indigo at a 2-in-6 duty cycle over transparent with the top 28% masked, which composites -- element screenshot, mean over the drawn box -- to rgb(195.5,192.5,246.0) = 1.71:1 on #ffffff and rgb(59.6,63.3,101.6) = 1.77:1 on #18181b. Against the eleven context columns that is a gap of 1.18:1 in light and 1.07:1 in dark, not fourfold. The current week's column is not the compliant mark the finding contrasts against the failing ones; by the finding's own 1.4.11 standard it is the worst offender on the chart, and the finding never sees it. THE FIX THEREFORE FAILS ITS OWN TEST AND INVERTS THE CHART. Applied as written and re-measured: the eleven history columns rise to 4.40:1 composited in light and 3.45:1 in dark (pure swatch 4.83:1 / 3.67:1 -- the finding's 3.68 is a rounding, not an error), while the one mark the whole surface is built around stays at 1.71:1 / 1.77:1, still under the floor. Visually the result is eleven heavy zinc-500 blocks with the running week as the faintest, most fragile thing in the frame -- context-versus-live flips from 1.18:1 to 2.56:1 in light and 1.07:1 to 1.95:1 in dark, with the darker mark now on the wrong side. The fix's stated justification, "the live column is darker (6.29:1), it is indigo, and it is hatched", is false on its first clause and internally inconsistent with its third: a hatch over paper cannot be 6.29:1, and this one is not. ON THE STRIP THE FIX MAKES THE READING WORSE. Repointing --disc flat drops the achromatic separation between past-a-fortnight and recent from 4.25:1 to 1.30:1 in light and from 3.50:1 to 1.62:1 in dark, leaving the strip's only real reading -- three jobs are sitting -- carried by hue alone. That is the one thing the palette lock names as forbidden: status and hierarchy are expressed by ink density, weight and fill, not by colour. The finding buys 1.4.11 on the six quiet dots by spending the CVD separation on the three that matter. The fix is also under-scoped: .meter i.zero at :339 is the same class of mark at the same 1.48:1 / 1.70:1 and is left alone, and it is the only mark in three of the first-run KPI cards; and in ?state=quiet the .dot.old count is 0, so all nine dots are quiet marks and no indigo appears in the strip at all -- a state the finding's consequence paragraph never reaches. Severity stands at defect for the underlying shortfall: the marks are visible to a normal-sighted reader at 1440, so visibly-wrong-but-passable is the right class -- but the seat's own case for it rests on a number that does not exist on this surface.
sharpenedFix: Keep the token -- --mark-quiet: #71717a in :root and in [data-v="dark"] is right, Ink 3 is in the locked eighteen and clears 3:1 in both grounds (4.83:1 / 3.67:1) -- then spend it differently. (1) STRIP, form not density: leave the six recent dots the quieter mark but carry the floor on a ring instead of a fill -- .dot::before { background: transparent; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px var(--disc); } with .dot { --disc: var(--mark-quiet) } and .dot.old::before { background: var(--disc) } restoring the solid fill at var(--accent). The 2px ring is the graphical object and clears 3:1; solid-versus-hollow is a fill difference, which is what the constraint sanctions, and it survives both CVD and reduced contrast sensitivity where a 1.30:1 luminance step does not. Re-point .dot:hover, .dot:focus-visible (:369) and .dot:active (:372) so they change the ring on a hollow dot rather than filling it, and leave .sk-wrap .dot::before (:457) its solid --wash so the loading state keeps its marks. (2) CHART, both marks or neither: do not repoint .bar on its own. If the eleven columns go to --mark-quiet, the current week must come with them -- raise the hatch to var(--accent) 0 3px, transparent 3px 6px in both .bar.part (:255) and the dark override (:263), keep the open top and the 1px accent rails, then re-measure the composited mean and confirm the current week still reads as the chart's dominant mark. It will not: a hatch over paper tops out near 1.73:1 whatever the duty cycle, so the honest conclusion is that the chart's compliance cannot be won by darkening the columns alone. Either give .bar.part a solid 1px Indigo 600/400 outline on left, right and bottom so the live week carries a 6.29:1 boundary as a delineated shape, or leave the columns at Ink 5 and argue the chart's case on its baseline, three valued gridlines and twelve dated ticks -- a weaker argument, but one the seat should make explicitly rather than assume. (3) Include .meter i.zero (:339) in whatever lands; it is the same mark at the same ratio. (4) Separately: .bar.live (:242) is dead in all seven states -- worth deleting, but that is the already-refuted dead-rules class, not this finding.
